newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen higher, Intel up.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen higher, Intel up.

text.p: High tech stocks are expected to lead Wall Street higher in early trading after a strong fourth quarter earnings report from Intel Corp.
Intel, which led a rally in technology issues on Tuesday before reporting its earnings after the stock market close, said its profits more than doubled during the quarter.
But analysts said it was not certain that high techs would be able to sustain their rally throughout the day, given their strong move on Tuesday.

"The futures are higher and Intel is higher in Europe. Intel will be the leader today," said Larry Wachtel, analyst at Prudential Securities. "That's as far as the opening is concerned. The question is sustainability and can the techs rally two days in a row."
Intel was up five at 152-1/2 in overnight trading in London. It reported fourth quarter earnings per share of $2.13, up from $0.98 a year ago. The First Call estimate had been $1.84.
Several other high techs followed Intel's lead and moved higher in London.
Investors will be keeping an eye on shares of major banks expected to report quarterly earnings today, including Fleet Financial Group Inc, BankAmerica Corp and PNC Bank Corp.
Wachtel said the fortunes of banking shares depended more on the bond market than on earnings reports, and banks have generally made a strong showing in the fourth quarter.
"Banks seem to move in accordance with the bond market," he said. "The earnings of the banks should be good, and the performance of their shares has been good."
The Tokyo stock market was closed Wednesday for a national holiday.
In London the FTSE 100 Index was down four points at 4165.
Among U.S. shares traded in London, International Business Machines Corp was up 1/2 at 68, Digital Equipment Corp gained 3/8 to 35-3/8, and Abbott Laboratories Inc was down 3/8 at 53.
The dollar was firmer but off its highs in Hong Kong. It was steady against the mark and yen in Europe.
U.S. Treasuries were up 6/32 to yield 6.76 percent.

The Wall Street Journal's "Heard on the Street" column says Wall Street is talking about yet another turnaround at Equitable Cos Inc. The company's shares were flat last year even as other life insurers soared.
The New York Times's "Market Place" column says U.S. public pension investors are eager to invest money in Shanghai, which is alive with entrepreneurial activity.
